builder_plan.scenario: Profiling shows attention computation is a bottleneck in your self-hosted service.
builder_plan.change: Check the supported GPU, tensor shapes, and precision, then replace only the relevant kernel.
builder_plan.baseline: The existing kernel inside the same complete serving pipeline.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Numerical differences, end-to-end latency, throughput, and memory at realistic shapes.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Taming Multi-Dimensional Skew in Sparse Matrix Multiplication with Contention-Aware Scheduling [Technical Report]
summary: It replaces static or single-metric load balancing in SpGEMM kernels with fixed-result-size morsels, contention-aware load balancing, SMT activation control, and per-morsel hybrid accumulation. Cost is added scheduler complexity and runtime overhead from dynamic morsel assignment and accumulator selection, with no stated accuracy or memory penalty. It can fail on workloads without meaningful skew, where gains vanish while scheduling overhead remains, and benefits may not transfer if the reader's sparse workloads run primarily on GPU rather than the CPU-style cache/SMT contention this targets.
rationale: The reader's sparse workloads on a single GPU are unlikely to hit the CPU cache-contention regime this targets, but if they run CPU-side graph or relational SpGEMM on skewed data, the scheduling framework is worth benchmarking against their current library.
technique: Contention-aware adaptive morsel scheduling for SpGEMM

claims.statement: It replaces static or single-metric load balancing in SpGEMM kernels with fixed-result-size morsels, contention-aware load balancing, SMT activation control, and per-morsel hybrid accumulation. Cost is added scheduler complexity and runtime overhead from dynamic morsel assignment and accumulator selection, with no stated accuracy or memory penalty. It can fail on workloads without meaningful skew, where gains vanish while scheduling overhead remains, and benefits may not transfer if the reader's sparse workloads run primarily on GPU rather than the CPU-style cache/SMT contention this targets.

Significantly outperforms state-of-the-art SpGEMM methods on skewed workloads with comparable performance on non-skewed ones, plus improved bandwidth utilization; the abstract gives no numerical factor.
